candidates.review_note: Build the undirected graph from the listed edge-disjoint paths. During an iterative depth-first search, every non-tree edge closes a cycle along ancestor tree edges. Mark those tree edges; if any was already in another fundamental cycle, the graph is not a cactus. A cactus passes because its cycles are edge-disjoint, while overlapping cycles force some tree edge to be marked twice. Each tree edge is climbed at most once before either completion or rejection, so the check is linear. Connectivity is checked separately. Bridges must be retained in a connected spanning subgraph; a cycle of length L allows retaining all edges or deleting exactly one of L edges, independently contributing L+1. Multiply with arbitrary-precision integers and enable long integer output. Preserve the original path input rather than inventing an edge-list interface.
